tagline.text: Pandan's crystal-clear river, named the cleanest inland waterway in the country

location.label: Location
location.text: Pandan, Antique (from the Malumpati Cold Spring area at the headwaters to Mag-aba on Pandan Bay)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500–2,000 (per person, estimate for transport, admission and meals; confirm locally)

children.text: The Bugang River is a clear river that flows across the town of Pandan in Antique into Pandan Bay. Thanks to residents' conservation work it has entered the national Hall of Fame for the cleanest inland body of water, and the Malumpati Cold Spring Resort near its source is the main attraction.
The Bugang River (known locally as Suba kang Bugang) lies in the municipality of Pandan, Antique, in northwestern Panay. According to Wikipedia it begins at an elevation of about

near the Northwest Panay Peninsula Natural Park and reaches the sea at the village of Mag-aba on Pandan Bay. From upstream to downstream it passes through the barangays of Candari, Santo Rosario, Guia, Zaldivar and Mag-aba, so it effectively crosses the whole town of Pandan. The watershed covers about 27.5 square kilometers. Sources differ on the river's length: the Wikipedia infobox gives about
while the text says about
6 km
, so think of it as roughly 6–10 km.

The river is known because its water is clear and villagers have protected it themselves. The Bugang River has won the national Cleanest Inland Body of Water award several times and entered its Hall of Fame, and in 2006 the UK-based Green Organization gave the Bugang Community-Based Eco-Tourism Organization a Green Environment Apple Award. In September 2014 the Philippine Senate passed a resolution commending Pandan's conservation efforts. The organization runs monthly cleanups and information drives and has also campaigned to ban riverside pigpens and swimming at the headspring.

For travelers the Bugang River is Pandan's leading attraction. The biggest draw is said to be the Malumpati Cold Spring Resort near the headspring, and downstream is Rosepoint Beach in Mag-aba, where the river meets Pandan Bay. White-sand beaches line Pandan Bay from Mag-aba to Duyong, and from Duyong Golden Beach you can see the Duyong Mountain Ranges and Batbatan Island. Pandan is about
55 km
from Kalibo and about
35 km
from Boracay, so many travelers stop here on the way to Boracay.

The research is interesting too. A survey from November 2013 to March 2014 recorded 38 fish species from 30 genera and 20 families in the river, the most dominant family being Eleotridae (6 species), followed by Gobiidae (4 species). In summer the water level sometimes drops temporarily. This guide draws mainly on two Wikipedia pages, and since no confirmed information was found on admission fees and opening hours, please check with the Pandan town tourism desk or a local information office before you go. When planning, think of Pandan not as a place to see many sights but as a place to feel clear water and the village's effort, and your expectations will fit. If Boracay's bustle has worn you out, a half day by the river and an evening on a quiet beach suits well, and it also works as one stop on a slow tour of northwestern Panay combined with Kalibo in Aklan or northern Antique.

A resort close to the source of the Bugang River, counted as Pandan's signature attraction. As the name says, cold spring water wells up here, a good place to cool off on a hot day. Opening hours and entrance fees vary by season, so check.

blocks.title: Cleanest inland body of water in the country

children.text: The river has been recognized several times in the Cleanest Inland Body of Water competition and has entered the Hall of Fame. This is the result of villagers cleaning and protecting it every month, so it is only polite for visitors not to leave trash.

The Bugang Community-Based Eco-Tourism Organization manages and guides visits to the river. In 2006 it received a Green Environment Apple Award from the UK-based Green Organization. Because it is run by villagers, visitors' respect matters.
A beach in Mag-aba where the river meets Pandan Bay. You can walk the mouth where fresh water meets the sea, and the view at sunset is lovely. Judge whether to swim by checking currents and waves.

White-sand beaches line Pandan Bay from Mag-aba to Duyong. From Duyong Golden Beach you can see the Duyong Mountain Ranges and Batbatan Island. It suits people who want to enjoy a beach more quietly than Boracay.
A survey recorded 38 fish species. Eleotridae and Gobiidae were the most common, and if you look into the clear water you will notice small fish. Do not feed or catch them; just watch.
Pandan's town fiesta, the Tugbong Festival, honors St. Vincent Ferrer and is held on
April 21–25
. It includes an agro-industrial fair, sports events, boat rowing and a beauty pageant. Dates may change from year to year.

The Leocadio Alonsagay Dioso Memorial Public Library in Pandan town is said to have been named by the National Library among the country's top libraries of its kind. If you have time, look around the building.
Set out from Kalibo or Boracay for Pandan. If you are coming from Boracay, it is better to leave early in the morning.
Arrive at the Malumpati Cold Spring Resort, see the clear water near the headwaters and rest in the cool spring water.
Have lunch at a nearby restaurant or from a packed lunch you brought.
Follow the river downstream and stroll at Rosepoint Beach in Mag-aba, taking in the view of the river mouth.
Watch the sunset and head back to Kalibo or Boracay.
Confirm the cold spring's opening hours and entrance fee locally. The distances are long, so also check the last departure times.

items.title: Full-day plan
items.subtitle: A day of river and beach

children.text: Arrive in Pandan and take a light look around the town plaza, the library and the market.
Go to the Malumpati Cold Spring Resort and spend time by the water near the headwaters.
After lunch, walk through village scenery along the middle reaches of the river and listen to the conservation organization's briefing.
Move to Mag-aba Beach and Duyong Golden Beach and enjoy the sea.
Watch the sunset and return to your lodging.
For a full-day plan it is easier to hire a vehicle for the day. Agree on the fare beforehand.
There are direct flights from Manila to Kalibo International Airport (KLO), taking about
1 hour
. Schedules change by season, so check when booking.
You could also use Caticlan Airport (MPH) on the Boracay side, but the route through Kalibo is more common for reaching Pandan.
According to Wikipedia, Pandan is about
55 km
from Kalibo. The usual way is to take a bus or van from Kalibo toward Antique and Pandan and get off in Pandan.
Confirm schedules and fares locally. Travel time varies with traffic.
The usual way is to leave Boracay for Caticlan and continue overland toward Pandan. Wikipedia says Pandan is about
35 km
from Boracay.
Many visitors stop here on the way to Boracay, so decide in advance where to leave your luggage and how long the trip will take.
From town to the Malumpati Cold Spring Resort or Mag-aba Beach, people go by tricycle, motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) or hired vehicle.
Confirm fares locally and agree in advance whether there is a ride back.

The dry season from December to May is clear and has little rain, which is good for outings by the river. In the dry season the water level sometimes drops temporarily, but the water looks clear and the weather is stable. In the rainy season the river rises and may carry muddy water, and roads may be slippery.

If you want to enjoy the beach too, hurry in the morning even within the dry season. If river activities are your focus, avoid the hot midday sun by using the morning and late afternoon, and after a rainy day ask locals about the water conditions before you move.

Pandan has small guesthouses and beach resorts. Unlike the big resorts of Boracay, they suit travelers who prefer a quiet beach, but choices are limited, so book ahead. Lodging on the beach side is around Duyong and Mag-aba, and prices and facilities change by season, so it is safer to check recent reviews.

Eat at restaurants in town and shops on the beach. Around Aklan and Antique you can easily find seafood and meat dishes such as grilled fish, squid, shrimp and roast chicken. Around the river and the cold spring, bring your own water bottle and lunch box to avoid making single-use trash. Take all your trash with you. At the local market you can buy seasonal fruit and snacks to eat by the river, but always take the peels and wrappers back with you.
Near the headwaters there may be conservation rules, so follow the signs.
Bring a towel, a change of clothes and a waterproof bag to rest comfortably at the cold spring.
Do not use single-use plastic bags or Styrofoam, and take your trash back.
Soap and sunscreen can pollute river water, so check before you go into the water.
If you are coming from Boracay, first check the travel time and the transport back.
Bring cash. In Pandan the ATMs are concentrated in town.
During the Tugbong Festival (late April) the town gets crowded and lodging may run short.
Because this is an activity run by villagers, respect the guides' words and the rules.
Upstream, do not make loud noise or play music, and ask first whether drones are allowed before filming.
If you travel with children, check the depth and current and bring life jackets.
A local campaign to ban swimming at the headspring is known to have existed. Be sure to follow the signs on site and your guide's instructions.
After rain the river can rise suddenly and the current can quicken, which is dangerous.
Sources differ on the river's length at 6–10 km, so the figures in this guide are approximate.
No confirmed information was found on entrance fees and opening hours, so check locally.
When entering the sea, check currents and waves, and wear a life jacket where one is needed.
Put valuables in a waterproof bag, and do not leave them on the beach while you go into the water.
